paragraphs: Transformers can process fewer tokens by merging similar representations, reducing computation and memory use. The challenge is deciding which tokens can be combined without losing useful information. Existing methods based on splitting tokens into two sets and matching them can depend heavily on that split and can damage informative representations in later layers.

PiToMe adds an energy score to guide these decisions. Tokens belonging to large groups of similar representations receive high energy and become candidates for merging. Tokens in smaller, more isolated groups receive low energy and are preserved. This gives the method a way to distinguish repeated information from unusual information that may deserve separate representation.

The experiments report reductions of 40–60% in floating-point operations, with smaller performance losses than comparison methods in image classification and image-text retrieval, alongside favorable results in visual question answering. The paper also establishes preservation of intrinsic spectral properties of the token space under mild conditions. Together, these results support token reduction that explicitly protects the structure and distinctiveness of the representations.
neurips-2024-accelerating-transformers-w.tldr: PiToMe accelerates transformers by merging redundant tokens while preserving distinctive representations and, under mild conditions, spectral structure.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can produce impressive image super-resolution results, but their memory and computational demands make deployment difficult. Binarization offers aggressive compression, yet applying existing methods to diffusion models substantially reduces performance. This paper addresses two sources of that difficulty: the network architecture and the changing behavior of its activations across diffusion steps.

BI-DiffSR uses a UNet designed specifically for binarization. Its downsampling and upsampling components maintain dimensional consistency and help transfer full-precision information. A separate channel-shuffling fusion component improves how features combine through skip connections. These changes adapt the paths through which information moves, rather than treating compression as an isolated replacement of numerical representations.

The method also introduces timestep-aware redistribution and activation functions. These adjust activation distributions at different diffusion steps, giving the binarized components more flexibility as the generation process evolves. Experiments show that BI-DiffSR outperforms existing binarization approaches. The stated result supports designing compression around both the architecture and the iterative behavior of diffusion models, rather than assuming that one fixed treatment works equally well throughout generation.
neurips-2024-binarized-diffusion-model-f.tldr: BI-DiffSR improves binarized image super-resolution by adapting both the network architecture and activation handling to diffusion models.

paragraphs: This paper estimates uncertainty associated with inputs outside a neural network's familiar data domain. It approaches the problem through the network's feature space, where inputs are represented as points. The central question is how deeply a new point sits within the distribution of those representations, providing a geometric basis for assessing unfamiliarity.

The method combines Lens Depth, a statistical measure of depth within a distribution, with Fermat Distance. Together, they measure the position of a point relative to the feature distribution without assuming a particular distributional form. The procedure has no trainable parameters and operates directly at test time, so it can be applied without changing the network's training process.

Because the uncertainty calculation leaves the original model untouched, the authors state that it does not affect that model's predictive performance. They report strong qualitative behavior on toy datasets and uncertainty estimates that can match or exceed strong baselines on standard deep learning datasets. The contribution is therefore a separate, training-independent uncertainty assessment whose reported competitiveness depends on the evaluated setting.
neurips-2024-combining-statistical-depth.tldr: Combining Lens Depth with Fermat Distance provides a parameter-free, test-time measure of out-of-domain uncertainty in neural network features.

paragraphs: The reversal curse describes a language model's difficulty using a learned fact in the opposite direction: learning that A is B may not enable it to answer that B is A. This paper investigates how that behavior changes across tasks and what it reveals about the mechanisms models use to recall and apply facts.

The authors find that reverse-direction generalization can occur when both relevant items appear in the context, as in a multiple-choice question. However, success is strongly associated with how the original fact was written during training. In the biography setting described, the effect appears for documents placing the name before the description, but not for documents placing the description before the name.

The paper proposes and verifies a hypothesis that models have an inherent bias in how they recall facts during knowledge use. This explains why document structure can affect later performance even when the underlying information appears equivalent. The authors also find that training alone has difficulty mitigating the bias's downstream effects. Their account makes reversal performance conditional on context and presentation, rather than treating it as a uniform inability.
neurips-2024-delving-into-the-reversal-c.tldr: Language models can reverse some learned facts, but success depends strongly on contextual cues and the structure of training documents.

paragraphs: When a machine learning model exceeds the memory of one device, computation must be distributed and information exchanged between devices. This paper develops a quantum-network framework that encodes data in specialized quantum states. Its central objective is to reduce the communication required for inference and gradient-descent training.

For models within this framework, the authors prove an exponential communication advantage over classical counterparts, with relatively modest overhead compared with standard gradient-based methods. The stated advantage holds regardless of data encoding cost. Certain graph neural networks fit the framework particularly well, and experiments provide evidence that these models perform well on standard benchmarks.

The framework can represent highly nonlinear input features, and its expressivity grows exponentially with depth. The paper also establishes a boundary: the exponential communication advantage cannot hold for linear classification. Finally, the authors suggest that limits on information extractable from transmitted quantum states may improve privacy. That privacy benefit is presented as a possibility, while the communication advantage is a theorem for the specified model class.
neurips-2024-exponential-quantum-communi.tldr: A quantum-network framework provably reduces communication exponentially for a specified class of distributed learning and inference models.

paragraphs: Diffusion-based combinatorial solvers often spend substantial computation repeatedly removing noise before producing a solution. Fast T2T trains a model to map different noise levels directly toward the optimal solution for an instance. Its optimization consistency objective encourages agreement among outputs from different generation trajectories and time steps, with the optimum serving as their shared target.

This training supports single-step generation while preserving the option to use multiple steps for better sampling quality. The method also adapts its search at test time. It updates latent solution probabilities using gradients of the optimization objective while alternating noise injection and denoising, helping the solver explore the solution space learned from historical instances.

Experiments on the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximal Independent Set report improvements in both solution quality and efficiency. Under limited time budgets, Fast T2T even outperforms LKH in the reported comparisons. With one generation step and one gradient-search step, it mostly exceeds diffusion-based counterparts requiring hundreds of steps while delivering speedups of tens of times. These are empirical results in the evaluated tasks and computational budgets.
neurips-2024-fast-t2t-optimization-consi.tldr: Fast T2T combines consistent direct solution generation with test-time gradient search to accelerate diffusion-based combinatorial optimization.

paragraphs: Federated learning can adapt pretrained vision-language models through prompts, reducing communication and computation. This paper asks why such adaptation succeeds or fails across diverse tasks. It develops a theoretical framework that follows two processes during learning: acquiring useful task signals and memorizing noise.

Within this framework, performance can be assessed through the ratio between coefficients associated with task-relevant and task-irrelevant information. The authors connect this distinction to portfolio optimization, where returns must be balanced against risk. That analogy motivates combining two prompts: a global prompt and a local prompt. The combination is intended to balance generalization with personalization rather than relying on either prompt alone.

The paper analyzes this prompt portfolio, demonstrates a performance advantage in its theoretical setting, and derives an optimal mixing coefficient. Experiments further support the theoretical claims. The contribution connects a practical design choice—how much global and local adaptation to combine—to an analysis of signal learning and noise memorization, providing a principled account of why a mixture can improve federated prompt learning.
neurips-2024-federated-learning-from-vis.tldr: A theory of signal learning and noise memorization motivates combining global and local prompts for better federated vision-language adaptation.

paragraphs: Adam's advantage over gradient descent is unusually large in language modeling. This paper identifies heavy-tailed class imbalance as a key contributor: word frequencies vary greatly, and gradient descent reduces the loss for uncommon words more slowly than for common ones. Because infrequent words collectively account for many samples, their slow progress can hold back the average loss.

The authors show empirically that this behavior also appears in vision convolutional networks and linear models, alongside language transformers. Reproducing it across these settings supports class imbalance as the underlying explanation rather than attributing the effect only to language-model architecture. Adam and methods based on gradient signs are less sensitive to the imbalance.

For a linear model trained with cross-entropy loss, the analysis connects imbalance to uneven, correlated gradients and loss curvature, properties previously hypothesized to favor Adam. A continuous-time proof further shows slow gradient-descent convergence on low-frequency classes without the corresponding slowdown for sign descent. The result provides both experimental and restricted theoretical support for class imbalance as one important cause of the optimizer performance gap.
neurips-2024-heavy-tailed-class-imbalanc.tldr: Heavy-tailed word-frequency imbalance helps explain Adam's advantage because gradient descent learns low-frequency classes more slowly.

paragraphs: Treatment effects can differ between groups whose boundaries are unknown in advance. Causal clustering seeks to discover such groups using information about outcomes under different treatments. This paper extends an existing approach based on k-means by introducing hierarchical and density-based alternatives for clustering unknown counterfactual regression functions.

The proposed estimators first estimate the relevant outcome functions and then apply readily available clustering algorithms. Unlike the earlier k-means formulation, they do not require its margin condition or strong structural assumptions on the outcome process. This broadens the kinds of subgroup structures that the causal clustering framework can accommodate while keeping the methods straightforward to implement.

The authors analyze convergence and show that, under minimal regularity conditions, the extra statistical cost of causal clustering is essentially the error in estimating the outcome regression functions. Simulations examine finite-sample behavior, and voting and employment projection datasets illustrate the methods. The framework also suggests applications to generic pseudo-outcomes. Its main contribution is a broader, theoretically analyzed route to identifying groups with similar treatment responses.
neurips-2024-hierarchical-and-density-ba.tldr: Hierarchical and density-based causal clustering discover treatment-response subgroups under weaker structural requirements than the k-means approach.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a scene from only a few views requires guidance about what unseen viewpoints should look like. Diffusion models can supply visual guidance, yet the paper argues that conventional Score Distillation Sampling struggles in this setting. Its analysis links the problem to mode deviation during optimization, associated with sparse views containing lower information entropy than text.

The proposed Inline Prior Guided Score Matching method uses relationships between camera poses to supply visual guidance within the reconstruction process. These inline priors rectify the distribution of rendered images and support a decomposition of the original optimization objective. This allows diffusion-based supervision without additional fine-tuning or pretraining.

The authors build an IPSM-Gaussian pipeline around 3D Gaussian Splatting and add depth and geometry consistency regularization. These components further improve the inline priors and the corrected rendering distribution. Experiments on multiple public datasets report state-of-the-art reconstruction quality. The approach matters because it makes viewpoint relationships part of how diffusion guidance is applied, directly addressing the optimization problem identified in the sparse-view setting.
neurips-2024-how-to-use-diffusion-priors.tldr: IPSM uses viewpoint relationships to correct diffusion guidance and improve sparse-view 3D reconstruction without extra model training.

paragraphs: Image-to-video diffusion models can generate less motion than intended. The authors attribute this tendency to conditional image leakage: at large diffusion time steps, the model relies too heavily on the input image. They address that dependency both when generating videos and when training the model.

At inference time, generation begins at an earlier time step to bypass unreliable large-time-step behavior. Analytic-Init supplies an initial noise distribution derived by minimizing its KL divergence from the actual marginal distribution, reducing the mismatch between training and generation. During training, TimeNoise applies noise to the conditioning image according to the diffusion step, using more noise at larger steps to weaken excessive dependence on that image.

The strategies are evaluated across several image-to-video models using an open-domain image benchmark collected by the authors and UCF101. Reported results combine higher motion scores with lower errors while preserving alignment with the input image and consistency over time. The findings suggest that controlling reliance on the conditioning image can improve both overall video quality and the accuracy of motion control.
neurips-2024-identifying-and-solving-con.tldr: Changing diffusion initialization and conditioning-image noise reduces excessive image dependence and improves motion in image-to-video generation.

paragraphs: Weighting observations changes how a predictor learns from pretrained features. This paper studies when those changes can be balanced by adjusting ridge regularization. It derives paths linking weighting matrices and regularization strengths so that different choices along a path produce asymptotically equivalent predictions against test vectors with bounded norms.

The equivalence requires weight and feature matrices with bounded operator norms and a technical relationship called infinitesimal freeness with respect to normalized trace functionals. The paths can be understood as matching the estimators' effective degrees of freedom. For subsampling without replacement, the results cover independently sampled random features and kernel features and confirm earlier conjectures about such equivalences.

The analysis also decomposes the risk of ensembles of weighted estimators. Along the equivalence paths, ensemble risks agree in the limit as ensemble size grows. Building on these results, the authors develop an efficient cross-validation procedure for tuning and apply it to subsampled pretrained representations across several models and datasets. The practical contribution follows from using proven relationships between weighting and regularization to organize model selection.
neurips-2024-implicit-regularization-pat.tldr: Under specified matrix assumptions, observation weighting and ridge regularization follow equivalence paths that enable efficient tuning of pretrained representations.

paragraphs: Lip reading converts visible mouth movements into text. Existing progress has largely relied on monolingual datasets, leaving a gap for people who switch languages within their speech. This paper introduces CSLR, a benchmark focused on Chinese-English code switching, to make that mixed-language setting available for systematic study.

The authors recruited 62 speakers proficient in both languages to produce sentences containing Chinese and English. After applying data-selection criteria, the collection contains 85,560 videos at a resolution of 1080 by 1920, covering more than 71.3 hours of lip movement. The dataset therefore provides a substantial collection centered specifically on language changes within the material being transcribed.

To establish benchmark results, the researchers evaluate commonly used lip-reading architectures and competitive methods from code-switching speech recognition. Their experiments identify CSLR as a difficult and underexplored task. The contribution is both the dataset and an initial evaluation framework: together, they support studying how visual speech systems handle bilingual utterances, extending evaluation beyond the monolingual settings emphasized by existing lip-reading resources.
neurips-2024-language-without-borders-a-.tldr: CSLR provides a large Chinese-English lip-reading dataset and benchmark for sentences that switch between languages.

paragraphs: An AI system personalizing its behavior must learn what a person values while avoiding harmful choices during that learning process. This paper investigates whether sharing more human-like representations helps. Its focus is representational alignment: how similarly humans and AI agents organize or judge relationships among possible actions.

The study begins with a theoretical prediction, examines human morality judgments, and then extends the investigation to ten aspects of human values, including ethics, honesty, and fairness. Agents learn in a multi-armed bandit setting, choosing actions and receiving rewards that reflect human judgments. This setup connects learning progress to the acceptability of the actions taken while exploring.

Using textual action descriptions, the authors collect human value judgments and similarity judgments from both people and multiple language models. They demonstrate that representational alignment supports safer exploration and better generalization in these personalization experiments. The finding gives shared representations a role beyond ordinary prediction accuracy: they can help an agent learn values through choices that better respect those values during the learning process itself.
neurips-2024-learning-human-like-represe.tldr: Human-like representations support safe exploration and better generalization when agents learn human values in personalization experiments.

paragraphs: Microscopy produces enormous amounts of image data, creating demand for models that can interpret biological images and communicate about them. Micro-Bench supplies an expert-curated evaluation resource for this capability. It covers 24 biomedical tasks across biology and pathology, multiple microscopy modalities, and scales ranging from subcellular structures to tissue.

The benchmark includes different organisms in normal and abnormal states. Evaluations of biomedical, pathology, and general-purpose vision-language models find difficulties across every task category, including basic distinctions between microscopy modalities. Models specialized through biomedical fine-tuning often perform worse than generalist models, showing that specialization alone does not ensure broader microscopy competence.

The authors also find that fine-tuning within particular microscopy domains can cause catastrophic forgetting, eroding biomedical knowledge already present in the base model. Interpolating the weights of pretrained and fine-tuned models offers one remedy and improves general performance across biomedical tasks. Released under a permissive license, Micro-Bench provides a shared way to examine both domain understanding and the tradeoffs that arise when adapting models to specialized biological imagery.
neurips-2024-micro-bench-a-microscopy-be.tldr: Micro-Bench exposes broad weaknesses in microscopy understanding and shows that specialized fine-tuning can erode existing biomedical knowledge.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to learn a near-optimal policy when a controlled dynamical system has low-rank latent structure. LoRa-PI alternates policy improvement with policy evaluation. During evaluation, it estimates a matrix whose entries describe the value of taking each action in each state under the current policy.

The matrix-estimation procedure has two phases. Uniformly sampled entries first support a spectral estimate of row and column leverage scores, which indicate their importance to the matrix structure. The algorithm then samples selected important rows and columns more closely and reconstructs the matrix using a CUR-like approach. This concentrates additional observations where they help recover the low-rank value function.

The authors establish entry-wise error guarantees that depend on matrix spikiness but not coherence. These yield a sample-complexity bound scaling with the sum of state and action counts and inversely with squared target error, alongside discount-factor and logarithmic terms. The bound is order-optimal in state count, action count, and accuracy under conditions milder than previous approaches. The result connects selective matrix sampling directly to efficient policy learning.
neurips-2024-model-free-low-rank-reinfor.tldr: LoRa-PI uses importance-guided low-rank value-matrix estimation to achieve order-optimal policy-learning sample complexity under milder conditions.

paragraphs: MV2Cyl reconstructs objects from multiple two-dimensional views as sketch-and-extrude CAD representations. This means recovering sketches and extrusion parameters that describe how the shape is built. The paper uses the images that commonly accompany 3D scans as a source of information about extrusion cylinders, processed through two-dimensional convolutional neural networks.

A central finding is that extracting extrusion surfaces alone produces suboptimal reconstruction. Occlusion and the difficulty of separating surfaces make that information insufficient for the best results in the study. MV2Cyl combines surface information with extracted base curves, bringing together evidence about the extrusion's boundary shape and its visible surfaces.

Experiments compare the method against earlier work that takes raw 3D point clouds as input. The authors report that combining base-curve and surface information gives their best reconstruction accuracy for both two-dimensional sketches and extrusion parameters. The contribution is a route from multiple images to structured CAD components, demonstrating that image evidence can effectively support recovery of the parameters needed for a sketch-and-extrude description.
neurips-2024-mv2cyl-reconstructing-3d-ex.tldr: MV2Cyl combines surface and base-curve evidence from multiple images to reconstruct sketch-and-extrude CAD representations.

paragraphs: Knowing a causal graph does not automatically reveal the strengths of its connections, especially when some variables are hidden. This paper asks when edge coefficients in a linear causal model can be recovered from partially observed data, assuming the causal structure is given. It considers all edges and allows flexible relationships among observed and latent variables.

The authors identify three types of parameter indeterminacy and derive graphical conditions sufficient for identifying all parameters. Some of those conditions are also proved necessary. This distinction matters: the work provides conditions that guarantee recovery without claiming that every sufficient condition must hold whenever recovery is possible.

The proposed likelihood-based estimator handles the variance indeterminacy of latent variables in a specific way. Its asymptotic recovery result identifies the underlying parameters up to trivial indeterminacy. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets support both the theory and the estimator's finite-sample effectiveness. Together, the results extend parameter analysis beyond connections between observed variables to the broader causal system, including relationships involving hidden variables.
neurips-2024-on-the-parameter-identifiab.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for recovering edge coefficients in partially observed linear causal models and develops a likelihood-based estimator.

paragraphs: Image inpainting fills missing regions, but agreement with a reference image does not directly express human aesthetic preference. PrefPaint trains an inpainting diffusion model using a reward learned from people’s judgments. The authors construct a dataset of nearly 51,000 images annotated with human preferences and use it to train that reward model.

Reinforcement learning then shifts the output distribution of a pretrained inpainting model toward higher predicted reward. The paper also derives an upper bound on reward-model error. This analysis addresses confidence in reward estimates during alignment and helps guide regularization, connecting the refinement process to the accuracy of the signal used to steer it.

Experiments cover inpainting comparisons and downstream tasks including image extension and 3D reconstruction. The authors report significant improvements in agreement with human preferences relative to state-of-the-art methods. The contribution combines a preference dataset, a reinforcement-learning procedure, and an analysis of reward accuracy, providing a framework for refining visual generation according to human aesthetic judgments.
neurips-2024-prefpaint-aligning-image-in.tldr: PrefPaint uses human-preference rewards and reinforcement learning to improve the aesthetic alignment of diffusion-based image inpainting.

paragraphs: SciCode evaluates whether language models can write code to solve real scientific research problems. Scientists and AI researchers contribute problems spanning 16 natural-science subfields, including mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, and materials science. The benchmark targets work that combines scientific understanding with programming, making the evaluation relevant to research assistance.

Its 80 main problems break down into 338 subproblems. Each subproblem involves recalling knowledge, reasoning about the task, and producing code. The benchmark also includes optional scientific background descriptions, scientist-annotated reference solutions, and test cases. This structure supports evaluating components of a research problem as well as the challenge of solving the larger task.

Among the models tested, OpenAI o1-preview performs best but solves only 7.7% of problems in the most realistic setting. That result indicates substantial remaining difficulty on this particular collection of research coding tasks. SciCode contributes a scientist-curated basis for examining progress toward useful scientific assistants, with problems and evaluation materials grounded in the combined demands of domain knowledge and executable solutions.
neurips-2024-scicode-a-research-coding-b.tldr: SciCode tests scientific research coding, with the strongest evaluated model solving only 7.7% of problems in its most realistic setting.

paragraphs: Model editing aims to update a language model's knowledge efficiently. Evaluations often emphasize whether the change succeeds, generalizes to related questions, and leaves nearby knowledge intact. This paper broadens the evaluation to the model's general capabilities after editing, comparing multiple editing methods and language models.

Across the evaluated methods, the authors report deterioration on general benchmarks. They conclude that general abilities are maintained only over small update sequences, on the scale of a few dozen edits, while larger sequences can disrupt or severely damage the model's internal knowledge structure. Instruction-tuned models show smaller general-knowledge losses, and larger models resist editing-related degradation better than smaller ones.

The evaluation also finds substantially weakened safety after editing, including in models that had undergone safety alignment. These findings support the paper's conclusion that the current methods examined are suitable only for small-scale knowledge updates. The broader contribution is to make preserved general competence and safety part of the assessment of an edit, alongside whether the targeted factual change works.
neurips-2024-should-we-really-edit-langu.tldr: Evaluated model-editing methods degrade general capabilities and safety as edits accumulate, with larger and instruction-tuned models showing greater resistance.

paragraphs: Language-model performance depends strongly on pretraining data, yet the datasets behind prominent open models are often unavailable and poorly documented. FineWeb addresses this gap with a public collection of 15 trillion tokens drawn from 96 Common Crawl snapshots. The authors report that models trained on it outperform models trained on other open pretraining datasets.

The work also documents and tests the decisions used to construct the collection. Detailed investigations examine deduplication and filtering, making dataset curation itself an object of study. These ablation experiments help connect choices about which web text to retain with the resulting language-model performance.

FineWeb-Edu is a 1.3-trillion-token subset selected for educational content. Models pretrained on it show dramatically better performance on knowledge- and reasoning-focused benchmarks such as MMLU and ARC in the reported evaluations. The release includes the datasets, curation code, and models trained during the ablations. Together, these resources support studying both large-scale web-data preparation and the performance effects of selecting text for particular informational qualities.
neurips-2024-the-fineweb-datasets-decant.tldr: FineWeb releases large, documented web-text datasets and shows strong language-model results from careful filtering, especially for educational content.

paragraphs: In a combinatorial semi-bandit problem, a learner repeatedly selects an action made up of base items and receives feedback about selected items. This paper develops algorithms that adapt to the statistical structure of those observations. In particular, correlations between item outcomes can inform decisions and improve regret, the accumulated cost of imperfect choices.

OLS-UCB-C uses online estimates of covariance structure, while COS-V uses variances alone. Both are optimistic algorithms with improved gap-free regret bounds, which do not require favorable separation between action values. COS-V draws inspiration from Thompson Sampling to reduce computational complexity, although its regret can be slightly suboptimal.

The authors establish a square-root-in-time gap-free regret bound for COS-V, up to polylogarithmic factors, and identify it as the first sampling-based algorithm with that guarantee. They also show cases where semi-bandit feedback improves on action-level bandit feedback even when the number of actions does not exceed the number of base items. The results connect structural adaptation with both stronger learning guarantees and practical computational considerations.
neurips-2024-towards-efficient-and-optim.tldr: Two adaptive semi-bandit algorithms use covariance or variance estimates to improve regret, with a sampling-based option reducing computation.

paragraphs: A node's importance in a changing network depends on when connections occur, not just which connections exist. Static measures such as closeness and betweenness can therefore give misleading answers. Temporal versions use shortest paths that respect the timing of interactions, but calculating those paths can be computationally expensive.

This paper investigates De Bruijn Graph Neural Networks as a way to predict temporal centrality from time-series graph data. The architecture is time-aware, making it suited to a task where the order of connections changes the meaning of a path. The aim is to estimate the relevant importance measures through learning rather than relying entirely on expensive path calculations.

Experiments cover 13 temporal graphs from biological and social systems. The approach substantially improves centrality prediction compared with a static graph convolutional network, an efficient sampling approximation for temporal betweenness, and two leading temporal graph-learning methods. The results support the value of a time-aware representation for predicting both temporal closeness and betweenness in the evaluated networks.
neurips-2024-using-time-aware-graph-neur.tldr: De Bruijn Graph Neural Networks improve predictions of temporal node importance across 13 biological and social networks.

paragraphs: Generating a new viewpoint from one image requires maintaining a plausible object shape despite incomplete visual evidence. Zero-to-Hero addresses inconsistencies and implausible views produced by Zero-1-to-3, particularly under difficult viewpoint changes. It operates during generation by modifying attention maps, without retraining the model.

The authors draw an analogy between diffusion denoising and stochastic gradient descent to motivate a filtering mechanism that aggregates attention maps. They also modify self-attention to incorporate information from the source image, reducing shape distortion. A specialized sampling schedule supports these changes. Together, the components improve how information is used throughout denoising while requiring no significant computational resources according to the abstract.

Experiments on diverse out-of-distribution objects show substantial improvements in fidelity and consistency. The authors additionally demonstrate the approach in multi-view generation and image generation conditioned on semantic maps and poses. The contribution is a test-time intervention that improves geometric consistency through attention processing, with reported applicability extending beyond the single-source novel-view setting that motivates the work.
neurips-2024-zero-to-hero-enhancing-zero.tldr: Zero-to-Hero improves novel-view fidelity and geometric consistency by filtering and modifying attention during generation without retraining.
